forecaster_note: If you're keen it will be worth going out in the morning for a wave. Small and clean, from traces of remaining south swell and a bit of NE wind wave. Probably best taking a log or something floaty. Later onshore and building — probably ending up blown out — as a strong S wind change comes through. – Surfline forecast team. Water temp is estimated (no live station feed this run).

wind.summary: Light WSW offshore till ~11am, then a strong S change — 32km/h gusting 43 by dusk.

shark.summary: Tagged White Shark #3654 detected by the North Steyne receiver at 12:22pm yesterday (Mon 14 Sep) — ~20h ago. That's the only real Northern Beaches detection in 24h; Dee Why, Long Reef and Curl Curl are clear. Feed is live (95 statewide detections in 24h, newest minutes old).

days.label: Today
days.note: Small, clean and fun-size early — 98% consistency but only ~49 kJ, so it's all shape and no punch. Light WSW offshore holds till around 11am, then a strong southerly change shuts it down. Go early or don't go.

dee-why.window: Dawn–10:30am. High tide 10:39am will fatten the Point — the earlier low-to-mid push is sharper.
alerts: Strong S change from early afternoon — blown out by 3pm

tip.label: Frontside call
tip.text: The 7s NE wind swell is the only real energy and it hits the beachies better than the Point. Take the frontside rights off the Point if there's a set bank working, otherwise walk north and milk the banks — keep your turns tight and drawn, there's nothing to lean on.

long-reef.window: Dawn–9am — wind goes cross-shore by mid-morning here, earliest window of the four.

tip.label: Pick of the bunch
tip.text: Best size and the NE swell lines up straight into it. Gets textured before the others though, so this is a dawn mission, not a 10am one.

curl-curl.window: Dawn–10am. Open beach, so it picks up the most of the NE swell — but also the first to go junky on the change.

tip.label: Bank hunt
tip.text: Exposed enough to get the full 3.6ft of NE wind swell. Shifty and quick — pick one bank and stay on it rather than chasing peaks.

manly.window: Dawn–11am — holds the offshore longest of the four, latest safe window.

tip.label: Backside option
tip.text: North Steyne lefts are backside for you — short, soft walls at this size, good for working on rail and fitting in turns rather than hunting a big hit.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Enormous but unsurfable for most. A 12ft @ 10s slab from dead south (183°) lands with ~2,556 kJ average and peaks over 3,000 — six times your usual big-day threshold — but it's short-period storm swell under 27–31km/h SSW wind. Size without shape. Sheltered southern corners are the only thing worth a look.

dee-why.window: No real window. Dead S at 183° wraps badly into Dee Why and the SSW wind is cross the whole day. Watch, don't paddle.
alerts: ⚠️ Dangerous size — 2,556 kJ average, 3,037 kJ peak
Dead-south swell direction — worst-case angle for Dee Why

long-reef.window: Closed out. Fully S-exposed, straight onshore, maxed beyond any rideable shape.
alerts: ⚠️ 8–15ft and blown out — not a surf, a spectacle

curl-curl.window: Closed out from first light. Nothing to hunt here.

manly.window: 6–10am is the only genuine option on the whole coast — the headland blocks the worst of it and the wind is offshore here.
alerts: Short-period swell won't wrap in cleanly — expect less size than the numbers suggest

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the day. Long-period S groundswell (18s and 14s) replaces the junk — real power in the sets but consistency drops to 70%, so expect long lulls between them. W offshore till ~11am, then SE. Sunday collapses to 45 kJ and knee-high; treat it as a write-off and plan around Saturday morning. Heads up: Friday 18th also looks light-offshore and clean if you can sneak out.

dee-why.window: Sat 6–11am is the window. Dead-S at ~180° again, so Dee Why sees the least of it — but it's clean and the long period gives the sets some shove. Sunday: 1–2ft, skip it.
alerts: Consistency only 70% — be patient, the sets are worth the wait
Sunday drops to 45 kJ — barely surfable

long-reef.window: Sat 6–11am — the standout of the weekend. Most S-exposed of the four, so it gets the full long-period swell with offshore wind on it.
alerts: Longer lulls than usual — sit wide and wait for the sets

curl-curl.window: Sat 6–10am. Picks up plenty of the S groundswell and the banks handle the longer period well.

manly.window: Sat 7–11am. Most sheltered from the S angle, so smallest of the four — only worth it if you want mellow.
